channel.title: Georgia Public Broadcasting - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Georgia Public Broadcasting (gpb.org)

item.title: Olympic-winning gymnast and Rockmart native Brody Malone speaks at Berry College
item.description: On Tuesday, Olympic bronze medalist and Rockmart, Ga., native Brody Malone spoke at Berry College as a guest lecturer.

item.title: WATCH: How traffic dried up in the Strait of Hormuz since the Iran war began
item.description: The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz is "about as wrong as things could go" for global oil markets. Iran achieved it not with a naval blockade, but with cheap drones.

item.title: There's a growing number of black vulture deaths by bird flu. That worries UGA researchers
item.description: University of Georgia researchers tested 134 dead black vultures from seven Southeast states including Georgia. They found more than 84% tested positive for bird flu.

item.title: Georgia Today: Property tax elimination; Endangered right whales; Protesting without a permit
item.description: On the Mar 4th edition: Georgia lawmakers reject a proposal to nearly eliminate property taxes for homeowners; Rules meant to protect endangered right whales are also now endangered; And a new bill seeks to make protesting without a permit a lot more expensive

item.title: Satellite images show Iran school strike hit more buildings than earlier reported
item.description: The images suggest that precision munitions struck other buildings, including a clinic that was also inside the complex.

item.title: Shifting rationales for strikes on Iran: White House says it doesn't want regime change
item.description: The Trump administration is sending mixed messages about regime change in Iran. It wants to remove the threat posed by Iran's leadership. Yet it's wary of another "endless war" in the Middle East.

item.title: Colossal Biosciences breeds controversy while trying to revive mammoths
item.description: A Texas biotech company is trying to bring mammoths and other extinct creatures back to life. The science is as intriguing as the ethical questions are thorny.

item.title: As Paralympics approach, U.S. skier Sydney Peterson balances training and research
item.description: Sydney Peterson is among the U.S. athletes heading to the 2026 Winter Paralympics. A neuroscientist in training, Peterson is studying movement disorders, similar to her own condition.

item.title: Carney says he backs strikes on Iran 'with some regret' as world order frays
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says he supports the strikes on Iran "with some regret" as they represent an extreme example of a rupturing world order.

item.title: A split Senate votes against measure to constrain Trump's authorities in Iran
item.description: Democrats in the Senate were facing an uphill climb Wednesday in their push to restrain President Trump's ability to wage war against Iran.
